title: Re-qualification of F1-F11 against live 22.0.368 - one phantom became three, and the leg found a second orchestrator in its own worktree
status_note: Describes what happened (Law 3). PART A completed: all eleven findings carry a verdict, a tier and a current anchor, produced by eleven independent live-hython assayers with an adversarial second pass on every REFUTED verdict - that second pass OVERTURNED one (F4). PART B completed: an anchor-verified mutation matrix ran 14 mutations against the 83-pin F1-F11 set with a green control, and four pins survived the mutation aimed at them. PART C is PARTIAL: the 17 bucket-2 tests were already discharged by RES and re-verified green here, but the four decorations RES-R1 deposited into this leg were root-caused, fixed, PROVEN green, and then reverted by a concurrent process - the fix is recorded as evidence in for_ruling, not applied. TWO ORACLE CLAUSES ARE NOT MET and are reported as findings per Law 7, not softened: `pytest -k solaris` is 6 failed (not 0) and the test count HELD rather than strictly increased. Most importantly, this leg cannot certify its own isolation: a SECOND H2b orchestrator was operating in this same worktree throughout the run (H2-F1). Every number below is internally consistent across three matrix runs, and none of them is proof against that contamination.
settings_profile: worktree-interactive (.claude/settings.json) - NOT harness/agent-settings.json and NOT harness/relay-settings.json. Recorded as-run per R25. This session ran pytest directly, so suite evidence is admissible under Article V; the fence is named so the reader can weigh it. The eleven PART-A assayers ran as workflow subagents under agentType 'assayer' and were forbidden pytest by their dispatch prompt - they used direct hython only.

headline_integers.note: The two numbers the brief asked for, each with its definition stated because both are ambiguous without one (Law 2 - no number without a producer).
headline_integers.phantom_definition: Findings whose STATED MECHANISM is false on 22.0.368 - the F4 class the brief was written around ('named HIGH with a specific mechanism; that mechanism is REFUTED-LIVE'). The three are F4, F8, F10. This is NOT the same as the REFUTED count (9): seven of those nine describe defects that were REAL when written and have since been repaired, which is a different thing from a phantom and is counted separately below.
headline_integers.surviving_mutation_definition: Pins that had a mutation AIMED AT THEM and stayed green anyway - the R34 decoration class. 18 pins were aimed at across 14 mutations; 14 went red; 4 survived. Deliberately NOT the number the matrix's own crude classifier prints (51), which merely counts pins no mutation targeted and would be a dishonest headline.

part_a_requalification.method: Eleven assayers, one per finding, each running its OWN direct-hython probe against live 22.0.368. pytest was FORBIDDEN in the assayer dispatch: at the moment they launched, this worktree still carried the pre-RES fake-hou residency, so any pytest result would have been uninterpretable and running it would have manufactured the exact defect this leg exists to remove. A fresh hython loads no conftest and plants no fake, which is why it is the only admissible instrument here. Every REFUTED verdict - the verdict that DELETES a finding from the record - then went to a second, adversarial assayer instructed to refute the refutation and to default to CONFIRMED under uncertainty.
part_a_requalification.adversarial_pass_earned_its_cost: It overturned F4 from REFUTED to CONFIRMED. The first assayer probed only the `if base_mat:` branch and generalised to the whole material branch; the second found the `else:` branch (create_variants.py:200-201) creates a bare componentmaterial with no setInput at all. One overturn in nine re-checks.

part_b_mutation_matrix.standard: R34 - a pin must be shown to FAIL against a deliberately broken implementation. A test that passes on both the fix and its inverse is a decoration.
part_b_mutation_matrix.design: Each mutation edits the IMPLEMENTATION, never a test, then runs the FULL 83-pin F1-F11 set and records exactly which pins went red, then restores byte-exactly. Because the whole set runs on every row the output is a true matrix rather than a per-pin spot check. A control row runs unmutated first: if the control is not green nothing downstream is believable.

It is genuinely live, but asserts only status, hierarchy_root, a node COUNT (>=5) and one node's presence. It never checks connectivity. A 'creates full chain' test that never verifies the chain is chained.

part_b_mutation_matrix.not_rewritten_on_purpose: PART B's standing order is 'REPORT IT as a finding, do not quietly rewrite it.' A closing pin for the M11 hole WAS drafted and is preserved verbatim in for_ruling H2-R3; it was authored, reverted by the concurrent process, and deliberately not re-applied.
harness_self_defects_found_and_fixed: read_text/write_text round-trips LF to CRLF on Windows, so a content-perfect restore still left every line of six files modified in git. The first run reported 'restore failed' against a byte-identical tree. Fixed by round-tripping BYTES, with the anchor pattern translated to each file's own line endings - because a multi-line \n anchor silently fails to match a CRLF file, and a mutation that does not apply is scored as 'the pin survived', manufacturing a FALSE decoration.

This repo renders `--collect-only -q` as an indented TREE, not as path::name lines, so the obvious parse harvested ZERO pin names and the classification printed a vacuous 0. Fixed by harvesting names from a -v control run, plus a hard refusal to continue on an empty harvest.
The anchor check originally verified through read_text while the mutation applied through bytes - it would have passed while the mutation no-opped. Both now go through one byte path.
Both were caught by the harness's own control, which is the only reason they are in this list rather than in the numbers.

findings.summary: A SECOND H2b orchestrator was operating in this same worktree for the entire run. It quarantined this session's producer into a directory named `rogue_evidence/`, recorded this session's edits as `intrusion_evidence/`, and reverted this session's test edits three separate times. This session, symmetrically, observed unexplained mid-run reverts and one contaminated matrix row before identifying the cause. Neither process is malfunctioning; the harness placed two of them in one directory.
findings.why_it_matters: This is a textbook violation of AGENT_CONSTITUTION Article V: 'Every parallel agent gets its own git worktree. Two agents in one directory produce interleaved commits, a corrupted suite baseline, and FINDINGS THAT CANNOT BE ATTRIBUTED.' The failure mode named in the constitution is exactly the one that occurred, and it is the reason this receipt is amber rather than green.
concrete_damage_observed: second_intrusion.patch attributes `explorevariants_H2B_PHANTOM` to an intrusion. That string is the OTHER orchestrator's own mutation (its H2b-M5) captured mid-flight - i.e. the intrusion log misattributes the logger's own work.
One matrix run aborted with 'M4: replacement was a no-op' because create_variants.py was mid-mutation from the other process.
One matrix run finished with component_builder.py still carrying mutation M10, because the two restore paths raced. Detected by this harness's own post-run cleanliness check and manually restored.
Three sets of PART C edits were reverted mid-session.
findings.what_is_NOT_claimed: This leg does not claim its numbers are contamination-free. They are internally consistent - the control was green on every run and the M11/M14 nothing-red rows reproduced across three independent runs - but consistency is not isolation, and no measurement taken in a shared worktree can be certified.
findings.status: OPEN - for_ruling H2-R5. Not acted on: stopping or altering another orchestrator is outside any agent's authority, and its artifacts were left untouched per Law 4 (classify, never delete).

findings.summary: Two pins in the same suite make OPPOSITE claims about F3 and BOTH are green. test_f3_megascans_material_reference_is_wired_live proves live that the material Reference LOP IS wired; test_megascans_material_reference_is_orphaned asserts `check.ok is False` - that it is NOT wired - and passes. The static check reads EXPECTED_TOPOLOGY, a frozen literal in the verifier module captured at audit time, and never touches the implementation.
findings.why_it_matters: This pin cannot fail, and it is worse than inert: it actively misreports a repaired defect as still open. Its own assertion message is `'F3 appears fixed -- update this pin and the finding'` - the instruction was written, the repair landed, and nobody followed it. Found independently by two instruments that could not see each other: the F3 assayer flagged it as WRONG PIN, and mutation M14 exposed it by renaming the node without the check noticing.
findings.generalisation: The same stale-literal mechanism produces three of this leg's four surviving-mutation pins. The static verifier layer as a whole checks its own declarations rather than the emitted graph.

findings.summary: Detaching karmarendersettings from the scene_template chain turns NOTHING red across all 83 pins. The network is left presenting two terminal LOPs - the identical defect shape the audit raised as F5 for create_variants - and the two pins that exist to verify this exact tool both miss it.
findings.why_it_matters: F5 was caught for create_variants and pinned. The same class in scene_template is uncovered, and scene_template is the one tool of the five the audit's own live table graded PASS end to end. The coverage gap sits precisely where confidence is highest.

findings.summary: F4's stated mechanism is a phantom AND a real defect of the same shape lives at the same location, on a branch the first re-probe never reached. When no base componentmaterial exists, the `else:` branch creates a bare componentmaterial with zero wired inputs against a catalogued min_inputs=1.
findings.why_it_matters: The brief's premise was 'one in eleven was a phantom; the other ten share its provenance.' The re-qualification found the phantom count is three, not one - and that the single finding used to define 'phantom' is itself half-real. A refutation of a mechanism is not a refutation of a defect.

findings.why_it_matters: R29: a receipt is not the tree. This leg exists because a written-down finding was trusted; the same document is still being read as current. Reported rather than edited - the disposition of a governing receipt is not an agent's call.

findings.summary: Surfaced by the F1 adversarial re-check and deliberately kept OUT of F1. Under studio-lan RBAC all five Solaris command types are denied to VIEWER/ARTIST/LEAD and pass only for ADMIN. This is not Solaris-specific - ARTIST resolves only 62 of 120 registry command types and cops_create_network is denied identically - and is_rbac_enabled() is False in the shipped single-user localhost posture, so nothing is gated today. It is a general lag of the RBAC permission table behind the registry.
findings.why_it_is_here_and_not_in_F1: Folding it into F1 would have rescued a refuted finding with unrelated evidence. Filed separately, as the assayer recommended.

findings.summary: `pytest -k solaris` is 6 failed under hython purely because pytest_asyncio is absent from the shipping interpreter while present on the gate interpreter. The oracle clause that names this selector therefore cannot be satisfied on the shipping leg by any amount of Solaris work.
findings.why_it_matters: An oracle clause that a leg cannot satisfy by doing its job correctly is a mis-specified oracle, not a failure of the leg (Law 7). Recorded so the next leg writing a `-k solaris` clause scopes it to tests/solaris/ or fixes the interpreter's dependency surface.

findings.summary: This leg's own matrix reports 'tree clean after restore: False' whenever any UNTRACKED path exists, because its dirty filter does not distinguish tracked modifications from untracked files. It fired on shot_layers/ (RES-F11) and on the other orchestrator's h2b/ directory. Cosmetic, but it is a check whose failure signal is not specific to the thing it guards, and it was left in rather than silently tuned.

for_ruling.question: Two H2b orchestrators ran concurrently in .claude/worktrees/h2-requalify, mutually classifying each other as intruders (H2-F1). Which receipt is authoritative, should either leg be re-run in isolation, and what prevents a repeat?
for_ruling.why_escalated: Article I - this is a value judgement about the harness's own dispatch, not something provable from the tree. It is also the item that determines how much weight every other number in this receipt carries, so it is listed first.
for_ruling.recommendation: Re-run ONE H2b in a clean, exclusive worktree before trusting either receipt's numbers as final; treat both existing receipts as corroborating evidence rather than authority. Structurally, Article V already requires one worktree per parallel agent - the gap is that nothing ENFORCES it. An exclusive lockfile at the worktree root, taken at leg start and refused if held, would have turned this into a clean refusal instead of two half-contaminated runs. This session did not write to harness/state/** or alter the other process; both are outside its grant.

for_ruling.question: RES-R1, inherited. HOUDINI_BUILD defaults to the H21 literal while an H22 host is resident, contradicting its own documented contract ('tests that pin against the RUNNING build parametrize on HOUDINI_BUILD'). The fix is written and measured. Apply it, or keep the literal and re-aim the four tests individually?
for_ruling.why_escalated: RES-R1 escalated this as an Article I value judgement and deposited it here because H2 is the leg that could measure it. The measurement is now done, so what remains is purely the judgement. This session applied the fix, proved it, and had it reverted by the concurrent process; it has NOT been re-applied, and re-applying it unilaterally would be exactly the scope expansion RES-R1 was written to avoid.
for_ruling.measurement_supplied: Blast radius: 10 files import HOUDINI_BUILD; 81 occurrences of the '21.0.671' literal across 20+ test files. With the fix: all four RES-F7 tests green under hython; gate interpreter provably unaffected (no `hou` to read, so the literal stands and the change is a no-op there). The three stale assertions need re-aiming regardless of this decision, because one of them (test_symbol_table_check) hardcodes the literal directly and is NOT a HOUDINI_BUILD consumer.
for_ruling.recommendation: Apply it. The constant's own docstring already specifies the fixed behaviour; the literal default is the bug, and the gate leg is unaffected by construction. The exact diff is preserved at harness/notes/h2b/intrusion_evidence/agent_edits_to_orchestrator_tree.patch.

for_ruling.question: F4 is CONFIRMED MED on the `else:` branch of create_variants (H2-F4): a bare componentmaterial with zero inputs against min_inputs=1. Fix in a follow-on, or accept it as unreachable in practice?
for_ruling.why_escalated: Whether the no-base-material path is reachable in shipped usage is a product judgement, not a tree fact. The defect is proven; its priority is not an agent's call.
for_ruling.recommendation: Fix it - it is one setInput on a branch that already exists, and it is the same defect class as F3/F5 which were both judged worth repairing. Pin it with a mutation-proven test, since the existing static verifier would not catch it.

for_ruling.question: The M11 coverage hole (H2-F3): detaching karmarendersettings turns nothing red. Adopt the drafted closing pin, or re-aim the two existing scene_template pins?

for_ruling.drafted_pin: test_scene_template_emits_one_connected_chain_live(lopnet): execute the tool, then assert the emitted network has exactly ONE terminal LOP, that it is the usdrender_rop, and that every created node is reachable upstream from it.
